# Shellfish

Shellfish in the HMI library has 565 reported results for lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid, monomethylarsonic acid, total mercury, methylmercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, Se, Ba, BTs_sum, DBT, DOT, DPT, MBT, MPT, NP-Hg, OTC_sum_as_Sn, PTs_sum, sumOTC, sumOTC (MBT+DBT+TBT+MPhT+DPhT+TPhT, as Sn), TBT, Tl, TMA, TPhT and TPT <li>
<strong>Main drivers:</strong>

Shellfish, as sold from Belledune Harbour East (HE), 1980 sampling (industrial-affected area) had cadmium higher at 62,300 µg/kg, against 3,850 µg/kg for Heron Island control site (HRI), 1980 sampling in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/chou-uthe1993-cadmium-american-lobster-belledune|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Chou CL, Uthe JF · 1993</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/chou-uthe1993-cadmium-american-lobster-belledune">Cadmium in American lobster (Homarus americanus) from the area of Belledune Harbour, New Brunswick, Canada: 1980-1992 results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Canadian Technical Report of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences No. 1916</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/chou-uthe1993-cadmium-american-lobster-belledune">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the shellfish came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-shellfish" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-shellfish-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of shellfish, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/chung2020-hong-kong-seafood-organotins" class="internal" data-slug="sources/chung2020-hong-kong-seafood-organotins" data-no-cite-meta>Chung et al. 2020</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach shellfish

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach shellfish comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Shellfish, as sold from water-soluble had TMA higher at 42,200 µg/kg, against 100 µg/kg for lipid-soluble in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kaise T, Hanaoka K, Tagawa S, Hirayama T, Fukui S · 1988</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Distribution of inorganic arsenic and methylated arsenic in marine organisms</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Applied Organometallic Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, shellfish, as sold from Belledune Harbour West (HW), 1980 sampling (industrial-affected area) had cadmium higher at 174,000 µg/kg, against 3,850 µg/kg for Heron Island control site (HRI), 1980 sampling in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/chou-uthe1993-cadmium-american-lobster-belledune|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Chou CL, Uthe JF · 1993</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/chou-uthe1993-cadmium-american-lobster-belledune">Cadmium in American lobster (Homarus americanus) from the area of Belledune Harbour, New Brunswick, Canada: 1980-1992 results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Canadian Technical Report of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences No. 1916</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/chou-uthe1993-cadmium-american-lobster-belledune">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

## Trade-offs and limits of controls

<a id="what-costs-constraints-adverse-effects-or-failure-modes-are-documented-and-which-are-unknown"></a>

Avoiding exposed growing areas lowered the metal measured in the studies available, but no study measured the cost or supply effect of doing so.<sup class="cite">[[sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kaise T, Hanaoka K, Tagawa S, Hirayama T, Fukui S · 1988</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Distribution of inorganic arsenic and methylated arsenic in marine organisms</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Applied Organometallic Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kaise1988-marine-organisms-arsenic-speciation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.

Reporting limits for lead ranged from 1 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food) to 2,000 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food), so a non-detect from a less sensitive method says much less.<sup <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-shellfish" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-shellfish" data-question="How do heavy metals get into shellfish?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into shellfish?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, shellfish from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than shellfish from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/chou-uthe1993-cadmium-american-lobster-belledune|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Chou CL, Uthe JF · 1993</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/chou-uthe1993-cadmium-american-lobster-belledune">Cadmium in American lobster (Homarus americanus) from the area of Belledune Harbour, New Brunswick, Canada: 1980-1992 results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Canadian Technical Report of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences No. 1916</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/chou-uthe1993-cadmium-american-lobster-belledune">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Shellfish, as sold from Belledune Harbour East (HE), 1980 sampling (industrial-affected area) had cadmium higher at 62,300 µg/kg, against 3,850 µg/kg for Heron Island control site (HRI), 1980 sampling in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/chou-uthe1993-cadmium-american-lobster-belledune|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Chou CL, Uthe JF · 1993</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/chou-uthe1993-cadmium-american-lobster-belledune">Cadmium in American lobster (Homarus americanus) from the area of Belledune Harbour, New Brunswick, Canada: 1980-1992 results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Canadian Technical Report of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences No. 1916</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/chou-uthe1993-cadmium-american-lobster-belledune">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-shellfish" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-shellfish" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in shellfish?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in shellfish?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, shellfish, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in PAHO (5.5 µg/kg) and the highest in AFRO (90 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in AFRO (18 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (300 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
